verdict.root_cause: The requests that actually error originate one hop downstream of checkoutservice, in the cart dependency. Every sampled PlaceOrder trace terminates at a CartService GetCart call inside prepareOrderItemsAndShippingQuoteFromCart, with the cart span the deepest ERROR and the checkoutservice handler, frontend gRPC client span and frontend HTTP span all inheriting it, while the intermediate prepare-items span carries no error of its own [tr_16a3c2fc03fd]. Failures return in about a millisecond, so nothing is waiting on a slow call [tr_16a3c2fc03fd], and checkoutservice's error ratio moved from a flat zero baseline to bursts peaking near 67% with repeated returns to zero [tr_931bfde32466]. The emailservice Ruby NoMethodError in the confirmation template [tr_dcd77519db4a] is a real but separate, non-fatal defect: checkoutservice logs it at warning severity and the order pipeline continues past it to a successful payment and message write [tr_0833eca9efea], and no email span appears in any erroring trace because the flow aborts at cart before confirmation is reached [tr_16a3c2fc03fd]. No dispatch touched cartservice at all, so I can name the failing service but not the failing mechanism.
verdict.reasoning: Span-level error attribution places the origin at the cart call and shows checkoutservice merely propagating it, which explains the simultaneous frontend and loadgenerator alerts without needing a second cause. Sub-millisecond error returns rule out latency or timeout as the mechanism [tr_16a3c2fc03fd]. The email 500s are excluded as the cause of the error-status requests because they are warning-severity and non-fatal to the order flow [tr_0833eca9efea] and never appear in the erroring traces [tr_16a3c2fc03fd]. Empty change logs for checkoutservice and emailservice [tr_f3d2531e02ff, tr_216b57dc45ee] remove those two as the acting service, but no cartservice evidence exists, so the mechanism class stays unknown rather than guessed.
open_questions: No cartservice logs, metrics, resource data or change history were collected — the actual mechanism (crash, OOM, backing-store refusal, bad rollout) is unestablished.
Metrics show episodic bursts returning to zero [tr_931bfde32466] while traces show uniform total failure [tr_16a3c2fc03fd]; the sampling windows differ and this conflict was never reconciled.

Whether the emailservice template defect and the cart failures share an upstream trigger, or are coincident and independent, is unresolved; both change queries also omit the hours before onset [tr_216b57dc45ee].

alternatives.root_cause: An emailservice template defect returning HTTP 500 on order confirmation degraded the checkout flow.
alternatives.why_not: The email failures are warning-severity and non-fatal — orders proceed to successful payment and message write past them [tr_0833eca9efea] — and no email span appears in any erroring trace because the flow aborts at cart first [tr_16a3c2fc03fd].

alternatives.root_cause: checkoutservice itself is faulty and generating the errors internally.
alternatives.why_not: The handler's error status is inherited from the child cart call and the service emits spans normally up to that point [tr_16a3c2fc03fd]; no change records exist for it in the window [tr_f3d2531e02ff].

proposal.expected_effect: No action is proposed, so the expected observable is continuation of the present state: checkoutservice error ratio keeps oscillating between 0 and ~0.67 with periodic threshold crossings on the same Prometheus query [tr_931bfde32466], and sampled PlaceOrder traces keep terminating at the CartService GetCart span with the cart span as deepest ERROR [tr_16a3c2fc03fd]. The correct next step is collection, not remediation: cartservice logs, restart/OOM counts, and a change-history query scoped to cartservice covering the hours *before* 15:49 onset. Any of those would either meet a precondition or name the mechanism.
proposal.if_wrong: This abstention is wrong if cartservice evidence turns up that meets an action's stated precondition — e.g. a recorded cartservice image or config change inside the window (making rollback_image or revert_config legal), or restart-count/OOM-kill evidence pointing at process state (making restart_service legal). It is also wrong if the failure escalates from episodic to sustained (error ratio pinned near its max with no returns to zero), where the cost of waiting exceeds the cost of a blind restart. Note that even the effect of a restart would be hard to read here: the metric already returns to zero on its own between bursts [tr_931bfde32466], so a post-restart zero could not be distinguished from the normal trough — an unfalsifiable success signal, and a further reason not to act yet.
proposal.risk: The risk of abstaining is prolonged partial checkout failure: at peak roughly two thirds of PlaceOrder calls error, and the last threshold crossing is at 17:28, near the window's end, so this is live and recurring [tr_931bfde32466]. Users continue to fail at cart lookup. The risk I am avoiding is larger: no dispatch touched cartservice, so restarting it would be an action on a service about which this investigation holds zero direct evidence. If the mechanism is a backing-store refusal or a bad rollout rather than process state, a restart discards cache, adds a cold-start error burst on top of an existing one, destroys the in-process forensic state that would have named the mechanism, and leaves the fault in place — and restart_service is marked irreversible.
proposal.blast_radius: None from this proposal, since nothing changes. For context on what a cartservice action would have touched: cartservice is reached from checkoutservice, and the error already propagates checkoutservice -> frontend gRPC client -> frontend HTTP [tr_16a3c2fc03fd], so a container recreate there would surface as connection resets to checkoutservice and as user-visible 500s at frontend and loadgenerator for the recreate duration — the same three alerted seeds already affected.

triage_judgement.reasoning: Critical alerts on checkout and frontend simultaneously with the load generator indicates a user-facing failure path, not a quiet system. No open incidents to attribute it to, and the shared checkout dependencies leave the cause open.
